shape_hint: A tall hexagon nut about 1.5 times the thread diameter in height, with a round flange/collar of diameter d1 and thickness a at one end (clamping fixtures, jigs, tooling); side view is a tall hex body on top of a thin disc collar.
notes: Chosen standard: DIN 6331 (collared, matches the Korean family name). DIN 6330 (plain 1.5d nut, spherical/ball seat form) has identical s, e_min and m for M6-M48; its extra dimension r (seat radius) is supported by 3 sources (schrauben-lexikon, boltsfastener, digipich) only for M6-M30: M6 9, M8 11, M10 15, M12 17, M16 22, M20 27, M24 32, M30 41 (M36 50, M42 58, M48 67 have only 2 sources) - not part of this table. Pitch column omitted (2 sources). KS B 1035 not verified. row_support = lowest per-column agreement (e_min and M48 rows have exactly 3 sources).

FE (fasteners.eu-derived): boltsfastener.com (same column set/order a,d1,da min/max,e min,m,s as fasteners.eu, no P column; its DIN 6330 page repeats fasteners.eu weights incl. comma decimals that differ from fasten.it)
German dataset: schrauben-lexikon.de (M6-M42 only; a,d1,m,s only - no e, no M48)

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 4 listed URLs + fasteners.eu live, HTTP 200. 12 rows x 5 value cols: fasten.it 60/60 ok, lexikon 44/44 ok (M48 absent, no e col), boltsfastener 60/60 ok, digipich 60/60 ok, fasteners.eu 60/60 ok. 0 mismatches. After clustering: s,m,d1,a rows M6-M42 = 3 clusters (fasten.it, lexikon, FE); e_min = 2 clusters (fasten.it, FE) ; M48 s,m,d1,a = 2 clusters (fasten.it, FE; lexikon lacks M48).
